metadata.title: Haskell Programming Language — Full Detailed Knowledge Graph
metadata.description: Interconnected, machine-readable explainer covering Haskell language design, functional programming, lazy evaluation, type inference, type classes, algebraic data types, monads and IO, syntax, runtime, compilers, standards, tooling, implementations, applications, history, and related languages.
metadata.source_basis: User-provided Haskell article text, with supplementary general Haskell ecosystem concepts marked in properties where appropriate.

entities.name: Haskell
entities.description: General-purpose, statically typed, purely functional language with type inference and lazy evaluation; named after logician Haskell Curry.

entities.name: Functional programming
entities.description: Organizes programs around function application, composition, immutable values, and transformations.

entities.name: Pure functional programming
entities.description: Ordinary functions avoid observable side effects; effects are represented explicitly as values and sequenced separately.

entities.name: Declarative programming
entities.description: Describes computations in terms of expressions and relationships rather than step-by-step mutation.

entities.name: Static typing
entities.description: Types are checked before execution, catching many invalid operations early.

entities.name: Strong typing
entities.description: Operations are constrained by types and explicit class/instance rules.

entities.name: Type inference
entities.description: The compiler infers types from expressions and constraints, historically based on Hindley–Milner inference.

entities.name: Lazy evaluation
entities.description: Expressions are evaluated when demanded, enabling incremental processing and potentially infinite structures, but complicating resource reasoning.

entities.name: Referential transparency
entities.description: A pure expression can be replaced by its value without changing program behavior.

entities.name: Immutability
entities.description: Values are not ordinarily modified in place; transformations construct new values.

entities.name: Higher-order functions
entities.description: Functions accept other functions as arguments or return functions.

entities.name: Lambda expressions
entities.description: Anonymous functions, commonly written with a backslash and parameter list.

entities.name: Recursion
entities.description: A function defines results through smaller or progressing instances of itself.

entities.name: Pattern matching
entities.description: Function equations and case alternatives choose behavior by matching data constructors and shapes.

entities.name: List comprehensions
entities.description: A concise notation for generating lists from sources with optional filters.

entities.name: Guards
entities.description: Boolean conditions select which function equation or alternative produces a result.

entities.name: Point-free style
entities.description: Defines functions through composition and combinators without naming all arguments.

entities.name: Function composition
entities.description: Combines functions so one function's output feeds another; commonly represented by the dot operator.

entities.name: Currying
entities.description: Represents multi-argument functions as a chain of single-argument functions.

entities.name: Partial application
entities.description: Applying fewer than all arguments creates a function awaiting the remaining arguments.

entities.name: Purity and effects separation
entities.description: Pure computations are separated from effectful actions represented as typed values.

entities.name: Type classes
entities.description: Named sets of operations implemented for types through instances, providing principled overloading and abstraction.

entities.name: Parametric polymorphism
entities.description: Functions and data types work uniformly over type variables, subject to constraints.

entities.name: Ad hoc polymorphism
entities.description: One operation name can have behavior selected by type, notably through type classes.

entities.name: Algebraic data types
entities.description: Types combine alternatives (sum types) and fields (product types), typically declared with data.

entities.name: newtype
entities.description: Creates a distinct type around one underlying representation, often with little runtime overhead.

entities.name: Type synonyms
entities.description: Aliases an existing type expression without creating a distinct nominal type.

entities.name: Type families
entities.description: Type-level functions associating types with other types; available through GHC extensions.

entities.name: Generalized algebraic data types
entities.description: Constructors can refine type variables to encode richer invariants.

entities.name: Kinds
entities.description: Classifies types and type constructors, including how type-level entities can be applied.

entities.name: Higher-kinded types
entities.description: Abstracts over type constructors, supporting classes such as Functor and Monad.

entities.name: Type signatures
entities.description: Declarations such as `f :: A -> B` document and constrain inferred types.

entities.name: Type constraints
entities.description: Requirements on type variables, commonly expressed through class constraints such as `Ord a => ...`.

entities.name: Modules
entities.description: Organize declarations and control imports/exports; hierarchical names such as Data.List are supported.

entities.name: Literate Haskell
entities.description: The .lhs format interleaves prose and code for documented programs.

entities.name: do notation
entities.description: Syntactic sugar for sequencing computations in monadic contexts, including IO.

entities.name: Monad
entities.description: An abstraction for sequencing context-bearing computations; used for IO, errors, state, parsing, nondeterminism, and other effects.

entities.name: Functor
entities.description: Maps a function over values inside a structure while preserving its shape.

entities.name: Applicative
entities.description: Models function application in a context and is more expressive than Functor but generally less sequencing-dependent than Monad.

entities.name: Foldable
entities.description: Abstracts over structures that can be reduced to an accumulated value.

entities.name: Traversable
entities.description: Abstracts traversal of a structure while sequencing effects and rebuilding the structure.

entities.name: IO
entities.description: Represents an effectful computation such as reading input or writing output; pure code can return an IO action.

entities.name: seq
entities.description: Creates a demand dependency between values and can help control laziness and memory use.

entities.name: Maybe
entities.description: Represents an optional value with Nothing or Just value.

entities.name: Either
entities.description: A sum type commonly used to represent failure or success explicitly with Left and Right.

entities.name: List
entities.description: Immutable lazy linked sequence with empty and head/tail constructors.

entities.name: Tuple
entities.description: Fixed-size product grouping values that may have different types.

entities.name: Eq
entities.description: Type class for equality and inequality.

entities.name: Ord
entities.description: Type class for ordering comparisons.

entities.name: Show
entities.description: Type class for converting values to human-readable text.

entities.name: Num
entities.description: Type class for common numeric operations.

entities.name: Integral
entities.description: Type class for integral numeric types and operations.

entities.name: Integer
entities.description: Arbitrary-precision integer type.

entities.name: Int
entities.description: Machine-sized signed integer with a bounded range.

entities.name: String
entities.description: Conventionally a synonym for a list of characters.

entities.name: Text
entities.description: Unicode text representation generally more efficient than lists of characters for text processing.

entities.name: ByteString
entities.description: Byte-oriented sequence for efficient binary data handling.

entities.name: Concurrency
entities.description: GHC supports lightweight threads and concurrent programs.

entities.name: Parallelism
entities.description: Suitable programs can execute computations across multiple CPU cores.

entities.name: Garbage collection
entities.description: Runtime memory management reclaims unreachable values; laziness and retained thunks affect residency.

entities.name: Thunks
entities.description: Deferred computations evaluated when demanded; retained thunks can contribute to space leaks.

entities.name: Space leak
entities.description: Unexpected memory retention, often caused by lazy computations retaining unevaluated work or references.

entities.name: Compiler optimization
entities.description: Transformations such as inlining, specialization, strictness analysis, and fusion can improve generated code.

entities.name: Fusion / deforestation
entities.description: Removes intermediate data structures between producers and consumers when safe and profitable.

entities.name: Strictness analysis
entities.description: Estimates which arguments must be evaluated and can enable efficient code generation.

entities.name: Glasgow Haskell Compiler (GHC)
entities.description: Main Haskell implementation, compiler and interpreter; supports native code, multiple platforms, and many type-system extensions.

entities.name: GHCi
entities.description: Interactive environment for evaluating expressions, loading modules, and experimenting with code.

entities.name: Cabal
entities.description: Build system and package format for Haskell libraries and programs.

entities.name: Stack
entities.description: Build tool associated with curated package sets and reproducible Haskell workflows.

entities.name: Hackage
entities.description: Online package repository for Haskell libraries and tools.

entities.name: Stackage
entities.description: Curated package snapshots used to improve dependency consistency and reproducibility.

entities.name: Foreign function interface
entities.description: Allows Haskell bindings to foreign code; the Haskell 2010 Report specifies C bindings.

entities.name: GHC extensions
entities.description: Extensions expand the language beyond the formal report and can be selected with LANGUAGE pragmas.

entities.name: Haskell 98
entities.description: Stable minimal portable language and library standard; originally published in 1999 and revised in 2003.

entities.name: Haskell 2010
entities.description: Formal language report published in July 2010, including hierarchical module names, FFI, pattern guards, inference changes, and LANGUAGE pragma specification.

entities.name: GHC2021
entities.description: Bundle of widely used GHC extensions released with GHC 9.2.1 in October 2021; not a formal language report.

entities.name: Haskell 2020
entities.description: Planned successor standard mentioned by the supplied source; the source does not establish it as a published formal report.

entities.name: Haskell Curry
entities.description: Logician after whom Haskell is named.

entities.name: Haskell committee
entities.description: Committee formed after FPCA '87 to define an open common non-strict purely functional language.

entities.name: FPCA '87
entities.description: Functional Programming Languages and Computer Architecture conference where consensus emerged to form the Haskell committee.

entities.name: Miranda
entities.description: Proprietary lazy functional language whose popularity helped motivate an open common standard.

entities.name: Clean
entities.description: Close relative of Haskell; uses uniqueness types for I/O and side effects rather than monads.

entities.name: Agda
entities.description: Functional language with dependent types and proof-assistant use cases; implemented in Haskell according to the supplied source.

entities.name: Elm
entities.description: Haskell-influenced functional language for web front-end applications with a narrower type-class model.

entities.name: Idris
entities.description: General-purpose functional language with dependent types.

entities.name: PureScript
entities.description: Haskell-inspired functional language that transpiles to JavaScript.

entities.name: Curry
entities.description: Functional/logic language based on Haskell.

entities.name: Bluespec SystemVerilog
entities.description: Haskell-derived hardware description language extension used for electronics design.

entities.name: Cryptol
entities.description: Language and toolchain for developing and verifying cryptographic algorithms, implemented in Haskell.

entities.name: Pandoc
entities.description: Tool for converting one markup or document format into another.

entities.name: xmonad
entities.description: Window manager for the X Window System written fully in Haskell.

entities.name: Darcs
entities.description: Patch-oriented revision control system written in Haskell.

entities.name: git-annex
entities.description: Tool for managing large data files under Git version control and supporting distributed synchronization.

entities.name: TidalCycles
entities.description: Live-coding environment for musical patterns embedded in Haskell.

entities.name: Cardano
entities.description: Blockchain platform whose node implementation is described by the supplied source as Haskell-based.

entities.name: seL4
entities.description: Formally verified microkernel project that used Haskell for prototyping and an executable specification before refinement to C.

entities.name: Semantic
entities.description: Haskell library for analyzing, diffing, and interpreting source code across programming languages.

entities.name: Haxl
entities.description: Haskell data-access library associated with Facebook and concurrent data fetching.

entities.name: Yesod
entities.description: Web framework for Haskell.

entities.name: Servant
entities.description: Haskell web/API framework for describing APIs with types.

entities.name: Snap
entities.description: Web framework written for Haskell.

entities.name: IHP
entities.description: Haskell web framework listed in the supplied source.

entities.name: Helium
entities.description: Educational Haskell dialect focused on clearer error messages, disabling type classes by default.

entities.name: Gofer
entities.description: Educational Haskell-like dialect developed by Mark Jones, known for constructor classes.

entities.name: Hugs
entities.description: Historical bytecode interpreter once widely used alongside GHC, now largely replaced by GHCi.

entities.name: Jhc
entities.description: Compiler emphasizing speed, efficiency, and program transformation research.

entities.name: Ajhc
entities.description: Fork of Jhc.

entities.name: Utrecht Haskell Compiler
entities.description: Research-oriented implementation supporting most Haskell 98 features and experimental extensions.

entities.name: nhc98
entities.description: Historical bytecode compiler emphasizing low memory use.

entities.name: York Haskell Compiler
entities.description: Historical nhc98 fork with goals including portability and a JavaScript backend.

entities.name: Eta
entities.description: Haskell dialect targeting the Java Virtual Machine.

entities.name: Frege
entities.description: Haskell-inspired dialect targeting the Java Virtual Machine.

entities.name: Disciple
entities.description: Strict-by-default Haskell dialect with explicit laziness and a type-and-effect system.

entities.name: Haskell community
entities.description: Community organizations, libraries, conferences, workshops, and hackathons sustain language development.

entities.name: Haskell Symposium
entities.description: Research and community event associated with ICFP.

entities.name: ZuriHac
entities.description: Haskell community event and hackathon in Zurich.

entities.name: International Conference on Functional Programming
entities.description: Conference associated with Haskell-related workshops and symposiums.

entities.name: Type-class laws
entities.description: Algebraic properties expected of well-designed class instances; laws are documented but not generally proved by the compiler.

entities.name: Property-based testing
entities.description: Tests general properties over generated inputs; useful for checking class laws and functional code.

entities.name: Formal methods
entities.description: Mathematical specification and verification; Haskell can act as a high-level executable model.

entities.name: Web development
entities.description: Haskell frameworks support web applications and typed APIs.

entities.name: Cryptography
entities.description: Haskell and Haskell-based tools have been used for cryptographic development and verification.

entities.name: Financial modeling
entities.description: The supplied source reports Haskell-like technology used in financial modeling.

entities.name: Systems software
entities.description: Haskell can be used for system tools and as a prototyping language for low-level systems.

entities.name: Data processing
entities.description: Functional transformations, folds, lists, and text/byte libraries support data processing.

entities.name: Source-code analysis
entities.description: Haskell has been used to implement source analyzers and developer tools.

entities.name: Hello World example
entities.description: Minimal program: `main :: IO (); main = putStrLn "Hello, World!"`.

entities.name: Factorial example
entities.description: Factorial illustrates recursion, pattern matching, guards, product, folds, point-free style, and fixed-point combinators.

properties.code:
factorial :: (Integral a) => a -> a
factorial 0 = 1
factorial n = n * factorial (n - 1)

entities.name: Quicksort example
entities.description: List quicksort illustrates pattern matching, Ord constraints, list comprehensions, recursion, and concatenation.

properties.code:
quickSort :: Ord a => [a] -> [a]
quickSort [] = []
quickSort (x:xs) = quickSort [a | a <- xs, a < x] ++ [x] ++ quickSort [a | a <- xs, a >= x]

entities.name: Haskell 2010 Language Report
entities.description: Formal report describing the Haskell 2010 language and library baseline.

entities.name: Real World Haskell
entities.description: Practical Haskell book listed in the supplied source.

entities.name: The Typeclassopedia
entities.description: Learning/reference resource focused on Haskell type classes.

entities.name: Cabal hell
entities.description: Historical nickname for dependency-resolution problems involving library versions; Stack and newer Cabal workflows responded to this problem.

entities.name: Nix-style build approach
entities.description: Build workflow idea associated with pinning inputs and reproducible dependencies; the source says Cabal borrowed ideas from Nix.

entities.name: GHC native code generation
entities.description: GHC compiles to native code on many processor architectures.

entities.name: LLVM backend
entities.description: GHC can use LLVM as a code-generation backend.

entities.name: C--
entities.description: Intermediate representation used by GHC in its compilation pipeline.

entities.name: Compiler pipeline
entities.description: Compilation involves parsing, typechecking, transformations, optimization, and backend code generation.

entities.name: Type error
entities.description: A mismatch among inferred and required types that prevents successful typechecking.

entities.name: Space reasoning
entities.description: Reasoning about retained values, strictness, allocation, and memory use is important in lazy programs.

entities.name: GHC lightweight threads
entities.description: GHC runtime supports lightweight threads and schedules concurrent work across CPU cores.

entities.name: State monad
entities.description: Models computations that thread state explicitly through a sequence.

entities.name: Parser monad
entities.description: Models parser computations and sequencing based on parsed results.

entities.name: Nondeterminism
entities.description: Models computations with multiple possible results or branches.

entities.name: Software transactional memory
entities.description: Transactional abstraction for coordinating concurrent state updates.

entities.name: Resource safety
entities.description: Ensuring files, sockets, and other resources are reliably released in effectful code.

entities.name: bracket pattern
entities.description: Resource pattern ensuring cleanup runs after use, including on exceptions.

entities.name: Haddock
entities.description: API documentation generator commonly used for Haskell projects.

entities.name: HLint
entities.description: Tool suggesting simplifications and style improvements in Haskell code.

entities.name: Haskell Language Server
entities.description: Editor integration for diagnostics, navigation, and code actions.

entities.name: REPL-driven development
entities.description: Interactive development workflow based on loading modules and evaluating expressions in GHCi.

entities.name: QuickCheck-style testing
entities.description: Property testing generates inputs to test general program properties.

entities.name: Rank-n types
entities.description: GHC extension allowing polymorphic types in additional positions.

entities.name: Existential types
entities.description: Type abstraction pattern that hides a type variable behind a constructor or interface.

entities.name: Deriving clauses
entities.description: Requests compiler-generated type-class instances for supported types.

entities.name: Record syntax
entities.description: Named data-constructor fields improve readability and field access.

entities.name: Monad transformers
entities.description: Compose effect abstractions such as state, errors, reader environments, and IO.

entities.name: MVar
entities.description: Synchronization variable used for communication and coordination in GHC concurrency.

entities.name: async package
entities.description: Library abstractions for asynchronous computations and concurrency management.

entities.name: Profiling
entities.description: Measures time and memory behavior to identify bottlenecks and space leaks.

entities.name: Benchmarking
entities.description: Measures program performance under controlled workloads.

entities.name: main
entities.description: Conventional program entry point, commonly of type IO ().

entities.name: map
entities.description: Applies a function to each list element.

entities.name: filter
entities.description: Keeps elements satisfying a predicate.

entities.name: foldr
entities.description: Folds a list from the right using a combining function and seed.

entities.name: foldl
entities.description: Folds a list from the left; strict variants can help avoid accumulator thunks.

entities.name: product
entities.description: Multiplies elements in a foldable structure.

entities.name: Maybe result
entities.description: Explicit representation of optional results instead of exceptions.

entities.name: Either result
entities.description: Explicit representation of success/failure results.
